mentions.name: Web-based music tracker
mentions.description: This website lets users make music through a tracker-style interface similar to FastTracker and OpenMPT. It is written in pure Rust using Leptos on the frontend (no JavaScript so far), with work so far focused on the music-making interface and backend development just beginning using sqlx. It has no manual, so use at your own risk.
mentions.source_excerpt:
I've been working on a music-making website since late spring. This is my first real frontend project, and I'm writing it in pure Rust using Leptos (so far, haven't had to write a single line of JavaScript!)

Most of my work so far has been on the actual music-making interface, but I'm beginning work on the backend now. I've only worked with Django before (for a school project at Georgia Tech), so I'll be deep in the `sqlx` documentation for a while.

There's no manual, so use at your own risk (it's similar to tracker programs like FastTracker and OpenMPT): https://mondobe.com/tracker

mentions.name: Web-based chiptune music tracker
mentions.description: A music tracker app (the '90s-style music-making software popular with chiptune artists) built with a Rust frontend using the Leptos framework, involving multithreading, audio playback, DOM interactions, and web workers with no JavaScript. The author plans to add a backend and potentially release it as a paid app.
mentions.source_excerpt: I'm getting into frontend web development with Rust by making a tracker [1] (not the advertising kind, rather a type of music-making app that was popular with chiptune artists in the '90s).
